2.08 Check a palindrome with constant extra space

Question

Improve the palindrome implementation so it does not allocate a cleaned copy of the string. Preserve the same English-letter and ordinary-space contract.

Answer

java
import java.math.*;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class Main {
    public static boolean isPalindrome(String text) {
        if (text == null) return false;
        int left = 0;
        int right = text.length() - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            char first = text.charAt(left);
            char last = text.charAt(right);
            if (first == ' ') {
                left++;
                continue;
            }
            if (last == ' ') {
                right--;
                continue;
            }
            if (Character.toLowerCase(first) != Character.toLowerCase(last)) return false;
            left++;
            right--;
        }
        return true;
    }

    private static int checks;

    private static void check(boolean condition, String description) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(description);
    }

    private static void rejects(Runnable action) {
        checks++;
        try {
            action.run();
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            return;
        }
        throw new AssertionError("Expected IllegalArgumentException");
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String[] inputs = {"madam", "Race car", "Never odd or even", "Java", "", null, "   ", " a ", " a b "};
        boolean[] expected = {true, true, true, false, true, false, true, true, false};
        for (int i = 0; i < inputs.length; i++) {
            check(isPalindrome(inputs[i]) == expected[i], "Palindrome input: " + inputs[i]);
        }
        System.out.println("PASS: " + checks + " checks");
    }
}

Detailed explanation

Step 1 Keep the original string

Use indexes into the input instead of creating a normalised copy.

Step 2 Skip a left-side space

Advance left and continue to the next iteration. The characters are read again at the new indexes rather than using stale cached values.

Step 3 Skip a right-side space

Decrement right and continue. These steps preserve the ordinary-space rule without allocating a second string.

Step 4 Compare normalised characters

Character.toLowerCase normalises each compared English letter. A mismatch returns false.

Step 5 Advance both indexes on a match

Every iteration moves at least one index, so the scan always makes progress and remains linear.

Walkthrough with input and output

Input Race carDecision
R versus rMatch after case conversion
a versus aMatch
c versus cMatch
e versus spaceSkip the right-side space
Indexes meet at eReturn true

Edge cases and tests

Null returns false. Empty, one-letter and space-only inputs return true. O(1) space refers to extra working storage: the original input still exists. This change improves memory use rather than the optimal O(n) worst-case time.

Additional explanation and complexity

The two indexes still move inward, but spaces are skipped directly in the original string. Character.toLowerCase() normalises each letter only when it is compared. continue starts the next loop iteration immediately. No cleaned copy is allocated.

The worst-case running time remains linear. A complete positive palindrome check needs to examine characters across the string.

Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) additional space.

2.09 Create an immutable Order with validation and notional

Question

Implement an immutable Order with orderId, symbol, int quantity and BigDecimal price. Initialise fields through the constructor. Reject null or blank identifiers, non-positive quantity and null or non-positive price using IllegalArgumentException. Provide getters and getNotional().

Answer

java
import java.math.*;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class Main {
    static final class Order {
        private final String orderId;
        private final String symbol;
        private final int quantity;
        private final BigDecimal price;

        public Order(String orderId, String symbol, int quantity, BigDecimal price) {
            if (orderId == null || orderId.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Order ID is required");
            }
            if (symbol == null || symbol.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Symbol is required");
            }
            if (quantity <= 0) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Quantity must be positive");
            }
            if (price == null || price.compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) <= 0) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Price must be positive");
            }
            this.orderId = orderId;
            this.symbol = symbol;
            this.quantity = quantity;
            this.price = price;
        }
        public String getOrderId() { return orderId; }
        public String getSymbol() { return symbol; }
        public int getQuantity() { return quantity; }
        public BigDecimal getPrice() { return price; }
        public BigDecimal getNotional() {
            return price.multiply(BigDecimal.valueOf(quantity));
        }
    }

    private static int checks;

    private static void check(boolean condition, String description) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(description);
    }

    private static void rejects(Runnable action) {
        checks++;
        try {
            action.run();
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            return;
        }
        throw new AssertionError("Expected IllegalArgumentException");
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Order order = new Order("O1", "AAPL", 10, new BigDecimal("100.25"));
        check(order.getOrderId().equals("O1"), "ID getter");
        check(order.getSymbol().equals("AAPL"), "Symbol getter");
        check(order.getQuantity() == 10, "Quantity getter");
        check(order.getPrice().compareTo(new BigDecimal("100.25")) == 0, "Price getter");
        check(order.getNotional().compareTo(new BigDecimal("1002.50")) == 0, "Notional");
        rejects(() -> new Order(null, "AAPL", 1, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order(" ", "AAPL", 1, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", " ", 1, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", null, 1, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", "AAPL", 0, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", "AAPL", -1, BigDecimal.ONE));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", "AAPL", 1, null));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", "AAPL", 1, BigDecimal.ZERO));
        rejects(() -> new Order("O1", "AAPL", 1, new BigDecimal("-1")));
        System.out.println(order.getNotional());
        System.out.println("PASS: " + checks + " checks");
    }
}

Detailed explanation

Step 1 Validate identifiers before assignments

Null or blank orderId and symbol values produce IllegalArgumentException before the object can be successfully constructed.

Step 2 Enforce quantity and price rules

The exercise requires positive quantity and positive non-null price. The price null check short-circuits before compareTo.

Step 3 Assign final fields once

this.field = parameter stores each validated value. Private final fields, a final class and no setters prevent the mutation paths relevant to this model.

Step 4 Check the types of stored values

String and BigDecimal are immutable and quantity is a primitive. These getters therefore do not leak mutable internal objects; a future List field would need additional care.

Step 5 Calculate and return notional

Convert quantity using BigDecimal.valueOf, multiply it by price and return the arithmetic result. The * operator cannot multiply a BigDecimal.

Walkthrough with input and output

Construction or callResult
O1, AAPL, 10, 100.25Construction succeeds
getNotional()100.25 times 10 becomes 1002.50
O1, AAPL, 0, 100.25IllegalArgumentException
O1, AAPL, 10, nullIllegalArgumentException before compareTo

Edge cases and tests

Test each constructor guard independently and verify that a valid object exposes the expected values. The rule rejecting non-positive prices belongs to this exercise; real instrument rules must decide whether negative prices are valid.

Additional explanation and complexity

The constructor validates values before assigning them. this.orderId means the field on the new object; orderId means the constructor parameter. Each call to new Order(...) creates an object with its own field values.

private prevents callers from directly accessing fields. final fields cannot be reassigned after initialisation. The final class prevents subclassing; no setters are provided. String and BigDecimal are themselves immutable, so these getters do not expose mutable internal objects. If the class later stores lists or dates, defensive copying may also be required.

BigDecimal.valueOf(quantity) converts the integral quantity into a decimal object. multiply() performs decimal multiplication and the method returns its result.

The positive-price rule is the contract of this exercise. Real instrument rules should define whether zero or negative prices are permitted rather than assuming one validation policy applies to every trading product.

Complexity: A constant number of fields is processed; decimal arithmetic cost depends on operand size.

Corrections discussed

  • quantity * price does not compile because BigDecimal does not support the multiplication operator.
  • A method declared to return BigDecimal must return a value on its normal path.
  • Constructor validation throws here because an invalid Order must not be successfully constructed. The earlier validation exercise instead collected all messages for a caller.
  • Use quantity < 0 when rejecting only negative quantities; use quantity <= 0 when zero is invalid too.

2.10 Deduplicate orders using equals and hashCode

Question

Two Order objects represent the same order when their orderId values match, even if other fields differ. Override equals() and hashCode(), then remove duplicate orders while preserving the first encountered object and its position. Assume valid non-null inputs and IDs.

Answer

java
import java.math.*;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.*;

public class Main {
    static final class Order {
        private final String orderId;
        private final String symbol;
        private final int quantity;
        private final BigDecimal price;
        public Order(String orderId, String symbol, int quantity, BigDecimal price) {
            this.orderId = orderId;
            this.symbol = symbol;
            this.quantity = quantity;
            this.price = price;
        }
        public String getOrderId() { return orderId; }
        public int getQuantity() { return quantity; }
        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object other) {
            if (this == other) return true;
            if (!(other instanceof Order)) return false;
            Order otherOrder = (Order) other;
            return Objects.equals(this.orderId, otherOrder.orderId);
        }
        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            return Objects.hash(orderId);
        }
    }

    public static List<Order> removeDuplicates(List<Order> orders) {
        Set<Order> uniqueOrders = new LinkedHashSet<>(orders);
        return new ArrayList<>(uniqueOrders);
    }

    private static int checks;

    private static void check(boolean condition, String description) {
        checks++;
        if (!condition) throw new AssertionError(description);
    }

    private static void rejects(Runnable action) {
        checks++;
        try {
            action.run();
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException expected) {
            return;
        }
        throw new AssertionError("Expected IllegalArgumentException");
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Order first = new Order("O1", "AAPL", 10, new BigDecimal("100.25"));
        Order second = new Order("O2", "MSFT", 20, new BigDecimal("50.00"));
        Order duplicate = new Order("O1", "AAPL", 99, new BigDecimal("101.00"));
        List<Order> result = removeDuplicates(List.of(first, second, duplicate));
        check(first.equals(duplicate), "ID-based equality");
        check(duplicate.equals(first), "Symmetry");
        check(first.equals(first), "Reflexivity");
        check(!first.equals(null), "Null comparison");
        check(!first.equals("O1"), "Different type");
        check(!first.equals(second), "Different ID");
        check(first.hashCode() == duplicate.hashCode(), "Equal values have equal hashes");
        check(result.size() == 2 && result.get(0) == first && result.get(1) == second,
                "Preserve first objects and their order");
        check(removeDuplicates(List.of()).isEmpty(), "Empty input");
        for (Order order : result) System.out.println(order.getOrderId() + " -> quantity " + order.getQuantity());
        System.out.println("PASS: " + checks + " checks");
    }
}

Detailed explanation

Step 1 Define business identity explicitly

This exercise treats matching orderId values as the same order even if quantities or prices differ. That is a chosen rule, not a universal definition for every order system.

Step 2 Handle identity and type safely

this == other returns true for the same object. instanceof rejects incompatible types and null before the cast.

Step 3 Compare the identity field

Objects.equals compares the two String IDs by value. The other fields are intentionally outside the chosen identity rule.

Step 4 Hash the same identity field

Objects.hash(orderId) gives equal orders equal hash codes. Hash collisions between different IDs are permitted; equality still decides whether an entry is a duplicate.

Step 5 Use an insertion-ordered set

LinkedHashSet suppresses equal later objects while retaining the original first object and encounter order. Converting it to ArrayList supplies the requested result type.

Walkthrough with input and output

Object encounteredID already presentKept object
O1 quantity 10NoFirst O1
O2 quantity 20NoO2
O1 quantity 99YesOriginal O1 quantity 10 remains

Edge cases and tests

Check reflexive equality, equal-ID symmetry, comparison with null and another type, equal hashes for equal IDs, empty input and preservation of the first actual object. Keeping the ID immutable avoids changing its hash behaviour while stored.

Additional explanation and complexity

this == other checks reference identity. instanceof rejects objects of other types and also returns false for null. The cast lets the method access Order fields. Objects.equals() compares the two IDs by value.

Hash-based collections use hash codes to locate candidate entries and equals() to determine equality. Equal objects must have equal hash codes; equal hash codes do not necessarily mean the objects are equal. Hash collisions are permitted.

LinkedHashSet removes equal objects while preserving insertion order. Constructing an ArrayList from the set returns the required list. The first O1 object remains, including its original quantity of 10.

super.equals() and super.hashCode() appeared in the starter as temporary object-identity behaviour. They must be replaced to implement the business identity rule.

Complexity: Expected O(n) time and O(k) space for k unique order IDs.

Source file: programs/10-order-equality/Main.java

2.11 Parse an HTML blotter and calculate executed BUY notional

Question

Extract rows from a table with ID blotter, map them to Trade objects and calculate price times quantity for EXECUTED BUY orders. The sample contains four trades. T1 contributes 100.25 × 10 = 1002.50; T4 contributes 25.50 × 20 = 510.00. The SELL trade T2 and PENDING trade T3 are excluded. The expected total is 1512.50.

The sample is a single-currency snapshot. HTML retrieval, JavaScript rendering, pagination and real HTTP calls are separate responsibilities.

This earlier HTML exercise is retained for completeness; it requires jsoup.

Answer

java
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.*;
import org.jsoup.Jsoup;
import org.jsoup.nodes.Document;
import org.jsoup.nodes.Element;
import org.jsoup.select.Elements;

public class Main {

    enum Side { BUY, SELL }
    enum Status { EXECUTED, PENDING, CANCELLED, REJECTED }

    // A record is a compact data holder. Access fields with trade.price(), etc.
    record Trade(String id, String symbol, Side side, Status status,
                 BigDecimal price, BigDecimal quantity) {}

    public static List<Trade> parseTrades(String html) {
        if (html == null || html.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("HTML must not be null or blank");
        }

        Document document = Jsoup.parse(html);
        Element table = document.selectFirst("table#blotter");
        if (table == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Blotter table is missing");
        }

        Elements rows = table.select("tbody > tr");
        List<Trade> trades = new ArrayList<>();

        for (Element row : rows) {
            Elements cells = row.select("td");
            if (cells.size() != 6) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Each trade row must have six cells");
            }

            String id = cells.get(0).text().trim();
            String symbol = cells.get(1).text().trim();
            Side side = Side.valueOf(
                    cells.get(2).text().trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
            Status status = Status.valueOf(
                    cells.get(3).text().trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT));
            BigDecimal price = new BigDecimal(cells.get(4).text().trim());
            BigDecimal quantity = new BigDecimal(cells.get(5).text().trim());

            if (id.isBlank() || symbol.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Trade ID and symbol are required");
            }

            Trade trade = new Trade(id, symbol, side, status, price, quantity);
            trades.add(trade);
        }

        return trades;
    }

    public static BigDecimal totalExecutedBuyNotional(List<Trade> trades) {
        return trades.stream()
                .filter(trade -> trade.side() == Side.BUY
                        && trade.status() == Status.EXECUTED)
                .map(trade -> trade.price().multiply(trade.quantity()))
                .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
    }

    private static int passed;
    private static int totalChecks;

    private static void check(String description, boolean condition) {
        totalChecks++;
        if (condition) passed++;
        System.out.println((condition ? "PASS: " : "FAIL: ") + description);
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        // Scope: one currency, fixed column order, no commas or currency symbols.
        // This fixture represents a rendered UI snapshot, not a live page.
        String html = """
            <table id="blotter">
              <thead><tr>
                <th>Trade ID</th><th>Symbol</th><th>Side</th>
                <th>Status</th><th>Price</th><th>Quantity</th>
              </tr></thead>
              <tbody>
                <tr><td>T1</td><td>AAPL</td><td>BUY</td><td>EXECUTED</td><td>100.25</td><td>10</td></tr>
                <tr><td>T2</td><td>MSFT</td><td>SELL</td><td>EXECUTED</td><td>50.00</td><td>20</td></tr>
                <tr><td>T3</td><td>GOOG</td><td>BUY</td><td>PENDING</td><td>12.00</td><td>5</td></tr>
                <tr><td>T4</td><td>AMZN</td><td>BUY</td><td>EXECUTED</td><td>25.50</td><td>20</td></tr>
              </tbody>
            </table>
            """;

        List<Trade> parsed = parseTrades(html);
        check("Parser extracts all four trades", parsed.size() == 4);
        check("First trade fields are mapped correctly", !parsed.isEmpty()
                && parsed.get(0).id().equals("T1")
                && parsed.get(0).symbol().equals("AAPL")
                && parsed.get(0).side() == Side.BUY
                && parsed.get(0).status() == Status.EXECUTED
                && parsed.get(0).price().compareTo(new BigDecimal("100.25")) == 0
                && parsed.get(0).quantity().compareTo(new BigDecimal("10")) == 0);

        BigDecimal actual = totalExecutedBuyNotional(parsed);
        BigDecimal expected = new BigDecimal("1512.50");
        check("UI total is 1512.50", actual.compareTo(expected) == 0);

        // Independent calculator checks let you practise TODO 2 before TODO 1.
        Trade buy = new Trade("B1", "AAPL", Side.BUY, Status.EXECUTED,
                new BigDecimal("0.10"), new BigDecimal("3"));
        Trade sell = new Trade("S1", "MSFT", Side.SELL, Status.EXECUTED,
                new BigDecimal("99"), new BigDecimal("10"));
        Trade pending = new Trade("P1", "GOOG", Side.BUY, Status.PENDING,
                new BigDecimal("99"), new BigDecimal("10"));

        check("Calculator includes an executed BUY exactly",
                totalExecutedBuyNotional(List.of(buy)).compareTo(new BigDecimal("0.30")) == 0);
        check("Calculator excludes SELL and PENDING orders",
                totalExecutedBuyNotional(List.of(buy, sell, pending))
                        .compareTo(new BigDecimal("0.30")) == 0);
        check("No matching trades returns zero",
                totalExecutedBuyNotional(List.of(sell, pending)).compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) == 0);
        check("Empty trade list returns zero",
                totalExecutedBuyNotional(List.of()).compareTo(BigDecimal.ZERO) == 0);
        check("Empty table returns no trades",
                parseTrades("<table id='blotter'><tbody></tbody></table>").isEmpty());

        System.out.println("Expected UI total: " + expected.toPlainString());
        System.out.println("Actual UI total:   " + actual.toPlainString());
        System.out.println("Checks passed: " + passed + "/" + totalChecks);
    }
}

Detailed explanation

Step 1 Parse the supplied snapshot

Jsoup builds a document from the HTML string. The parser checks that the required table exists before selecting rows.

Step 2 Select body rows and validate width

tbody > tr excludes the header row. The six-cell check runs before indexed access so a missing field does not silently shift every subsequent value.

Step 3 Extract and convert fields

text().trim() gets cell content. Enum conversion normalises recognised labels, and BigDecimal parses the decimal strings directly.

Step 4 Create one domain object per row

Parsing returns all four rows, including SELL and PENDING orders. It does not discard data based on a calculation-specific rule.

Step 5 Filter and calculate separately

The calculator keeps EXECUTED BUY records, multiplies each price by quantity and reduces the notionals from zero. This separation lets another adapter supply the same domain objects later.

Walkthrough with input and output

TradeParsedIncluded in totalContribution
T1 BUY EXECUTEDYesYes1002.50
T2 SELL EXECUTEDYesNo0
T3 BUY PENDINGYesNo0
T4 BUY EXECUTEDYesYes510.00

Total: 1512.50.

Edge cases and tests

An empty supported table returns an empty trade list and zero total. Missing columns, invalid decimal text and unknown labels should not be silently ignored. This version assumes fixed column order, supported formatting and a complete same-currency snapshot; jsoup does not execute browser JavaScript.

Additional explanation and complexity

Jsoup.parse(html) creates a searchable document. selectFirst("table#blotter") locates the table. table.select("tbody > tr") identifies data rows. row.select("td") identifies cells. text().trim() extracts cell text. In the fixed-column practice version, indexes 0 through 5 mean ID, symbol, side, status, price and quantity.

Side.valueOf() and Status.valueOf() convert normalised strings into enums. Locale.ROOT makes case conversion independent of the machine's default locale. new BigDecimal(cellText) converts prices and quantities directly from their decimal representation. Each row produces a new Trade that is appended to the result list. The parser returns all trades; the calculator applies business filters.

The validation checks reject missing HTML, a missing table, an incorrect cell count and blank identifiers. Invalid numbers and unknown enum labels also throw exceptions. This simplified parser assumes the supplied column order and table structure.

filter() keeps executed buys. map() computes each notional. reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add) adds the values and returns zero for no matches. BigDecimal quantity supports fractional quantities in this model.

Complexity: parsing depends on the HTML input size; the calculation is O(n) for n trades, apart from decimal operand costs. The parsed model uses O(n) space.

Reusable parser variation

The earlier full TradeBlotter implementation accepts a table selector and maps header names to column indexes. It tolerates reordered columns, rejects duplicate trade IDs, validates supported statuses and positive quantity, and adds row numbers to row parsing errors. Nested tables and merged cells are outside its contract. Numeric strings use a dot decimal separator without grouping commas or currency symbols. Signed prices are allowed in that full model; instrument rules should determine restrictions.

Its source, HTML fixture, 32-check runner and readme are in programs/12-html-blotter/. The complete OneCompiler program above is in programs/13-onecompiler-blotter-complete/Main.java. The original practice snapshots and Maven dependency configuration are in practice/onecompiler/.

JSON comparison follow-up

The sample summary JSON contains currency GBP and executedBuyNotional "1512.50". A JSON parser and live API reconciliation were proposed as the next exercise, but were not implemented in the previous chat. Compare totals numerically with compareTo() after agreeing currency, units, filters, rounding, pagination coverage and snapshot time. Matching totals alone do not establish that every individual trade matches.

2.12 Reusable HTML parser with header mapping

Question

Variation: build a reusable parser that accepts a table selector, locates columns by header name, maps rows to Trade objects and calculates executed BUY notional. Support reordered columns and report invalid rows clearly. Agree a duplicate-ID policy and a supported table/number-format contract.

Answer

This is the full reusable HTML parser originally supplied, including its domain model and Streams calculator. The complete runnable project and check runner are included in programs/12-html-blotter/.

java
import org.jsoup.Jsoup;
import org.jsoup.nodes.Element;
import org.jsoup.select.Elements;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.*;

/** Java 17+. All rows must belong to the same currency and snapshot. */
public final class TradeBlotter {
    public enum Side { BUY, SELL }
    public enum Status { NEW, PENDING, PARTIALLY_FILLED, EXECUTED, CANCELLED, REJECTED }

    public record Trade(String id, String symbol, Side side, Status status,
                        BigDecimal price, BigDecimal quantity) {
        public Trade {
            if (id == null || id.isBlank() || symbol == null || symbol.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Trade ID and symbol are required");
            }
            Objects.requireNonNull(side, "side");
            Objects.requireNonNull(status, "status");
            Objects.requireNonNull(price, "price");
            Objects.requireNonNull(quantity, "quantity");
            if (quantity.signum() <= 0) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Quantity must be positive");
            }
        }

        public BigDecimal notional() {
            return price.multiply(quantity);
        }
    }

    public static final class HtmlTradeParser {
        private static final Set<String> REQUIRED = Set.of(
                "trade id", "symbol", "side", "status", "price", "quantity");

        public List<Trade> parse(String html, String tableSelector) {
            if (html == null || html.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("HTML is required");
            }
            if (tableSelector == null || tableSelector.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Table selector is required");
            }

            Elements matches = Jsoup.parse(html).select(tableSelector);
            if (matches.size() != 1 || !matches.first().tagName().equals("table")) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Selector must identify exactly one table");
            }
            Element table = matches.first();
            // This adapter deliberately supports simple tables, not nested or merged cells.
            if (!table.select("td table, th table, [colspan], [rowspan]").isEmpty()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Nested tables and merged cells are unsupported");
            }
            Elements headerRows = table.select("thead > tr");
            if (headerRows.size() != 1) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Exactly one header row is required");
            }
            Elements headers = headerRows.first().children();
            Map<String, Integer> columns = new HashMap<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < headers.size(); i++) {
                String name = headers.get(i).text().strip().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
                if (!headers.get(i).tagName().equals("th") || name.isBlank()
                        || columns.putIfAbsent(name, i) != null) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid or duplicate table header: " + name);
                }
            }
            if (!columns.keySet().containsAll(REQUIRED)) {
                Set<String> missing = new TreeSet<>(REQUIRED);
                missing.removeAll(columns.keySet());
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Missing headers: " + missing);
            }

            List<Trade> trades = new ArrayList<>();
            Set<String> ids = new HashSet<>();
            Elements rows = table.select("tbody > tr");
            for (int i = 0; i < rows.size(); i++) {
                try {
                    Elements cells = rows.get(i).children();
                    if (cells.size() != headers.size()
                            || cells.stream().anyMatch(cell -> !cell.tagName().equals("td"))) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell count or structure differs from header");
                    }
                    Trade trade = new Trade(
                            text(cells, columns, "trade id"),
                            text(cells, columns, "symbol"),
                            Side.valueOf(text(cells, columns, "side").toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)),
                            Status.valueOf(text(cells, columns, "status").toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)),
                            new BigDecimal(text(cells, columns, "price")),
                            new BigDecimal(text(cells, columns, "quantity")));
                    if (!ids.add(trade.id())) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate trade ID: " + trade.id());
                    }
                    trades.add(trade);
                } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Blotter row " + (i + 1) + ": " + e.getMessage(), e);
                }
            }
            return List.copyOf(trades);
        }

        private static String text(Elements cells, Map<String, Integer> columns, String field) {
            String value = cells.get(columns.get(field)).text().strip();
            if (value.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Blank field: " + field);
            }
            return value;
        }
    }

    public static BigDecimal totalExecutedBuyNotional(List<Trade> trades) {
        return trades.stream()
                .filter(trade -> trade.side() == Side.BUY && trade.status() == Status.EXECUTED)
                .map(Trade::notional)
                .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);
    }
}

Detailed explanation

Step 1 Identify exactly one supported table

The selector must find a table. Unsupported merged cells or nested tables are rejected so the parser cannot misinterpret their structure.

Step 2 Build the header index

Trim and normalise each header and map its name to its current index. Duplicate headers and missing required names fail before row parsing.

Step 3 Validate and map every row

Require the row width to match the headers, then look up each field by its header index rather than a fixed hard-coded position.

Step 4 Apply validation and identity rules

The domain constructor validates required data and positive quantity. A Set tracks IDs so duplicate trade rows cannot accidentally double the total.

Step 5 Report context on failure

The row loop wraps parsing failures with the one-based row number. Invalid records fail clearly rather than disappearing from a financial calculation.

Step 6 Return the parsed model and aggregate separately

List.copyOf returns an unmodifiable list structure. The independent calculator uses the same domain type and business filters as the simple parser.

Walkthrough with input and output

HeaderOriginal indexExample reordered index
Trade ID04
Price45
Quantity50

Header lookup changes the indexes, so the same trade values are extracted after the columns move.

Edge cases and tests

Test reordered columns, missing and duplicate headers, malformed row width, invalid enums/numbers, duplicate IDs and zero matching orders. The adapter intentionally rejects unsupported table shapes and locale-dependent number formats instead of guessing.

Additional explanation and complexity

The header map translates each required field name to its current column index. Every row is converted into a validated domain object. Duplicate IDs and malformed rows fail clearly. The calculation operates independently of extraction. Complexity is linear in the parsed input and processed cells, apart from decimal operand costs, with storage for the DOM, trades, headers and IDs. The runnable parser project includes the existing 32-check runner.

3.02 Compiler errors and collection pitfalls

If versus if

Java keywords are case-sensitive. An uppercase If may cause a misleading "; expected" message. Write if.

Class and filename must match

Save public class Main in Main.java, or public class Order in Order.java. Class names contain no spaces. If renaming a class, also update its constructor and all corresponding type references.

Compile and run commands differ

text
javac FindDuplicateTrades.java
java FindDuplicateTrades

The compiler command needs the .java filename; the run command uses the class name. An error saying "Class names, 'FindDuplicateTrades', are only accepted if annotation processing is explicitly requested" commonly means a bare class name was passed to javac instead of a source filename. Enabling annotation processing is not the fix for that filename mistake.

Missing Collectors import and wrong stream element type

java
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

List<String> ids = counts.entrySet().stream()
        .filter(entry -> entry.getValue() > 1)
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
        .collect(Collectors.toList());

Without map(Map.Entry::getKey), this stream produces a list of entries, not strings. Even with the mapping, an unordered HashMap does not satisfy the earlier second-occurrence ordering requirement.

Interface versus implementation

java
List<String> result = new ArrayList<>();
Set<String> ids = new HashSet<>();
Map<String, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();

List, Set and Map are interfaces; create a concrete implementation. Arrays.asList() is fixed-size. List.of() and Map.of() are unmodifiable and reject nulls. new ArrayList<>(input) makes a separate list structure; it is a shallow copy, not a deep copy of contained objects.

Comparison types

Use equals() for String content, == for enum constants and primitive comparisons, and compareTo() for numeric BigDecimal comparisons. Integer references compared with == may compare object identities; do not rely on integer caching for value comparison.

OneCompiler dependency runs

The HTML exercise needed Add Dependencies and a pom.xml containing jsoup 1.24.1. In that session, the top Run button used Maven, while the file-context Run action bypassed dependency setup. Maven compiled other Java files too, exposing an older class/filename mismatch. The supplied practice pom includes only Main.java so the blotter exercise can run independently. A public Main entry point was needed for that Maven setup.

Core Java exercises need no jsoup dependency. In a workspace retaining the restricted practice pom, use Main.java for the selected exercise or adjust the build configuration deliberately.

3.03 Oral interview questions and short answers

Objects

  • "An immutable Order validates its inputs, prevents reassignment, exposes no mutation operations and does not leak mutable internal state."
  • "Two equal objects must have equal hash codes. Equal hash codes alone do not establish equality."
  • "A final reference cannot be reassigned, but the referenced object's contents may still be mutable."
  • "Object is the root class; Objects is a null-safety and equality utility class."

References: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/lang/Object.html and https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Objects.html

Collections

  • Why use entrySet() when both key and value are needed? It exposes each pair directly rather than requiring another lookup by key.
  • Does HashMap preserve insertion order? No; choose LinkedHashMap when that is the requirement.
  • Can a mutable order be used as a key? Only if changes cannot affect its equality/hash behaviour while stored; an immutable ID key is usually simpler.
  • Why does Arrays.asList().add() fail? The returned list has fixed size.
  • Is an unmodifiable collection deeply immutable? No; contained mutable objects may still change.

References: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Collection.html and https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Map.html

Streams

  • map transforms each input; flatMap transforms and flattens nested results.
  • collect builds a result container; reduce combines elements into a value under its algebraic contract.
  • A parallel stream is a performance choice, not a thread-safety mechanism.
  • Comparator.comparing(Trade::notional).reversed().thenComparing(Trade::tradeId) means descending notional and ascending ID; the model must define those accessors.

References: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/stream/Stream.html and https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/stream/Collectors.html

Concurrency

  • A volatile counter can still lose increments because count++ is a compound operation.
  • AtomicLong protects a single counter; it does not make an entire order-processing transaction atomic.
  • shutdown() initiates orderly shutdown; awaitTermination() waits; shutdownNow() is an interruption attempt, not a forced kill.
  • Consistent lock ordering helps prevent deadlock. Limit lock scope and avoid remote calls while holding a shared lock.
  • Clean ThreadLocal values and release resources in finally or an appropriate resource-management construct.

References: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/package-summary.html and https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/util/concurrent/ExecutorService.html

Additional follow-ups

  • Rewrite duplicate detection using two sets instead of a frequency map.
  • Rewrite totals.put(symbol, totals.getOrDefault(symbol,0) + quantity) using merge().
  • Explain the difference between || and && in null-safe validation.
  • Explain why discarded BigDecimal.add() results do not update a total.
  • Confirm currency, filters, units and snapshot alignment before comparing UI and API totals.

3.04 Other prompts preparation plan and role context

Other prompts mentioned

The preparation discussion also mentioned maximum contiguous subarray sum (Kadane's algorithm), second-largest array values, moving zeros, reversing words, financial ratio services, asynchronous status polling, bounded execution, pipeline optimisation, memory leaks, heap versus stack, and Java keyword / HTTP / wait-strategy recall. These were topic suggestions; no worked Java program for those topics was supplied in the previous chat.

An earlier maximum-subarray prompt was: given an integer array, return the sum of its contiguous subarray with the largest sum. Follow-ups included explaining the brute-force approach and complexity before optimising, and handling all-negative arrays.

Seven day practice plan discussed

Day 1: collections, strings and equality. Day 2: objects, validation and exceptions. Day 3: Streams, grouping and financial values. Day 4: unit tests and testable design. Day 5: API automation and BDD. Day 6: asynchronous systems and code review. Day 7: a timed mock and review of weak areas. The suggested routine was revision, independent coding, tests and an explanation aloud.

For each coding exercise, restate the requirement, clarify ambiguous behaviour, walk through an example, select a data structure, implement a simple solution, test boundaries and discuss complexity and maintainability.

The readiness discussion recommended attempting fresh strings, arrays and collections exercises independently under a 25-minute limit, with compilation, edge-case tests and an explanation of complexity. The recommendation to request additional time was based on the practice shown at that point, not a prediction of the interview outcome.

Role and source context

The practice was tailored to the Test Director / Head of Test Automation context, with emphasis on Java, trading data, automation design, BDD, APIs, CI/CD and distributed-system reliability. Public interview guides were treated as topic leads rather than proof of exact director-round questions. PracHub displayed HTML parsing and maximum-subarray prompts as practice material. Glassdoor could not be independently retrieved during the check. A separate SMBC developer vacancy supported the relevance of Java, APIs, concurrency and automated testing, but was not the target role's interview specification.
